note: user_current_paths is a config-less redirect module (no settings, permissions, plugins, schema, or Drush). It defines three login-required routes: /user/edit -> current user's edit form; /user/current -> /user/{uid}; /user/current/{wildcardaction} -> /user/{uid}/{wildcardaction}. The controller substitutes the current user's id for 'current' and validates the target with path.validator (invalid -> 404). It also adds an 'Edit my account' link (weight -9) to the 'account' menu. Because there is no per-site config, medium introspection cases create a namespaced test user with a FIXED uid and ask what /user/current/... resolves to for that account (the agent must look up the uid on the live site), and hard cases build a menu_link_content in the account menu that targets one of the module's UID-neutral paths, verified against live state.

evals.prompt: What URLs does the Drupal user_current_paths module add, and what does each one do for the logged-in user?
evals.expected_output: It adds three login-required routes: /user/edit redirects to the current user's edit form; /user/current redirects to /user/{uid} (the current user's canonical page); and /user/current/{action} redirects to /user/{uid}/{action} (e.g. /user/current/edit, /user/current/cancel). It also adds an 'Edit my account' link to the account menu.

evals.prompt: In the user_current_paths module, how does /user/current/{action} decide where to send the user, and what happens if the resulting path is not a valid or accessible route?
evals.expected_output: The controller replaces 'current' with the current user's uid to build /user/{uid}/{action}, then validates it with the core path.validator service (getUrlIfValid). If it is a valid, access-checked route it redirects there; otherwise it throws NotFoundHttpException (404). Access checks on the target still apply.

evals.prompt: The user_current_paths module adds a menu link for logged-in users. What is the link's title, which menu is it in, and which path does it point to?
evals.expected_output: It adds a static menu link titled 'Edit my account' (weight -9) to the 'account' menu, pointing at route user_current_paths.edit_redirect (/user/edit), which redirects to the current user's edit form.

evals.prompt: This site has a user account with the email ucp_known@example.com. Given how the user_current_paths module works, if that specific user visited /user/current/edit, what exact path would they be redirected to? Inspect the live site to determine the account's user id.
evals.expected_output: The account ucp_known@example.com has uid 900169, so user_current_paths replaces 'current' with 900169 and redirects /user/current/edit to /user/900169/edit.

evals.prompt: A user account with email ucp_alt@example.com exists on this site. Using the behavior of the user_current_paths module, what path does /user/current (with no action) resolve to for that user? Inspect the live site to find the user id.
evals.expected_output: The account ucp_alt@example.com has uid 900170; /user/current has a default action of 'view', so it redirects to the canonical user page /user/900170 (no /view sub-path exists).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, add a link to the 'account' (user) menu that takes the logged-in user to their own profile page using the UID-neutral path provided by the user_current_paths module (/user/current). Create and save the menu link on the live site.
evals.expected_output: Create a menu_link_content entity in menu 'account' whose link uri is internal:/user/current (a path provided by user_current_paths that redirects to the current user's /user/{uid} page).

evals.prompt: On my Drupal site I want a menu item in the user account menu that lets whoever is logged in go straight to the page for deleting/cancelling their own account, without me hard-coding a specific user. The user_current_paths module provides a path for this. Add that menu link and save it.
evals.expected_output: Create a menu_link_content entity in menu 'account' whose link uri is internal:/user/current/cancel, which user_current_paths redirects to /user/{uid}/cancel (the current user's account cancel page).
